entries.note: Informed readers would measure 'minimal utility, minimal value' in different ways. The separate 'likely transient fad' part is probability language and is rightly left out.

entries.test: Whether, once LLMs are widely useful, a handful of big tech firms (Microsoft, Google, Amazon, Meta) take a cut from essentially all LLM-based apps and services through model or cloud fees.
entries.note: The antecedent ('if generative AI proves useful') is loose. 'Parasitic' is a loaded word, but the claim underneath about control and fees can be tested.

entries.test: Reported 2024 generative AI revenues versus costs and losses at the leading providers, and whether a few firms had locked up the LLM market.
entries.note: The factual premise (gen AI loses far more than it makes) can be checked. Whether the 'monopoly worked' is vaguer.
The 'master plan' is his own hypothesis about big tech's goals. Readers would not agree on what would count as it 'falling apart'.

entries.test: Whether big tech companies' later revenue growth comes substantially from generative AI products and services.
entries.note: It looks ahead to whether gen AI will drive growth, so it is a forecast. The Meta/Google decade claim uses 'may' and is rightly left out.
